Hi Caroline / Samir,

Following our MAP cadence, attaching the updated MAP workbook (acme_map_v3.xlsx) and the latency summary PNG from the sprint runs. This thread is to capture our weekly checkpoint specifically on the performance benchmarking workstream (latency & throughput) and to confirm next-step owners and timing ahead of your EVAL window.

Status (quick):
- MAP phase: Evaluation — system benchmarking
- Close timeline we agreed: target decision week of 2026-07-12 (final commercial close by 2026-07-19)
- Current blocker: discrepancies between our internal staging runs and the numbers obtained in your cloud account for large-batch workloads.

Key asks for this checkpoint:
1) Caroline: confirm the test cluster spec you used (instance types, concurrency, seq len) so we can reconcile numbers.
2) Redwood: share consolidated p50/p95 latency and sustained throughput profiles from staging and canary.
3) Owners: map tuning experiments to owners + expected completion dates.

Proposed next steps (we'll cover these in the 11:00 PT sync):
- Rishi to present the consolidated benchmark (p50/p95, tokens/sec, max sustainable QPS) and variance across model variants.
- Sergio to propose batching/quantization experiments and a quick canary rollout plan.
- Vanessa to update MAP timeline and runbook, push required Docs to the shared Drive folder.

Thanks Vanessa — I uploaded our raw run logs to the Drive folder and added a short note about the cluster specs. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Test cluster: 8x NVIDIA T4 (g4dn.xlarge equivalent), multi-tenant dev subnet (not isolated).
- Concurrency: we ran with 6 worker threads, batching enabled with a max_batch_size=16; sequence length averaged 512 tokens for these runs.
- Observed throughput: sustained ~1800 tok/s across the cluster, but p95 latency spiked to ~860ms on some bursts.

Samir flagged a concern that our environment may be noisier than your dedicated staging; happy to stand up an isolated node if that helps. Also, would appreciate a short note on what you consider the acceptable p95 target for the evaluation — is 600ms acceptable for the customer P0 flow?

Caroline Jensen

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP checkpoint — performance benchmarking deep dive

On Tue, Jun 29, 2026 at 09:02 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following our MAP cadence...

Hi all — posted the consolidated benchmarking table below (also in latency_summary_q2.png). Numbers come from our dedicated staging cluster (pinned GPU queue) using the same model checkpoint you intend to evaluate. Runs were repeated 5x, averages reported: 

- Model: redwood-7b-v1 (fp16)
- Seq len distribution: median 256, 95th pct 512

Results (staging):
- p50 latency (single request, cold): 42ms
- p95 latency (steady load, 16 batch): 430ms
- Sustained throughput: 2,600 tokens/sec (single node)
- Max sustainable QPS (end-to-end): 210 QPS (multi-node horizontal)

Discrepancy notes vs Acme runs:
- Your multi-tenant dev subnet likely yields higher tail due to co-located noisy neighbors (explains p95 spikes).
- Batching config matters: our default continuous batching window was 12ms for these runs; increasing window to 20ms raised throughput but also increased p95 by ~10%.

Tuning experiments I propose and owners: 
1) Batching window sweep (5/12/20ms) — owner: Rishi — deliverable: table of p50/p95 vs tokens/sec — ETA 2026-07-02
2) Quantization quick test (int8 dynamic) on a single node — owner: Sergio — deliverable: delta in latency and quality (sample prompts) — ETA 2026-07-03
3) Isolated canary run in Acme account (single pinned instance) — owner: Acme infra (Samir) with Redwood runbook — deliverable: raw logs + reconciled numbers — ETA 2026-07-01

Action: Grace, can you draft a short fallback policy for the MAP (auto-fallback to lower-capacity model variant + routing to a cheaper region) we can include in the MAP workbook?

I'll present these items in the 11:00 sync and capture any live adjustments.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Staff SRE, Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference

Next meeting: same time next week (Tue 11:00 PT) — tentative agenda: reconciled canary logs + tuning results.
